doc.title: David Friesen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2024

title: Music as showing forth the glory of God; childhood faith
summary: Friesen says he plays to show God's glory; raised by a Christian father and Russian Jewish mother, he was given freedom of choice, and he describes his faith.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I was going to start off with — I have the Grove Dictionary of Jazz and the All Music Guide to Jazz and you are mentioned in both of them. And I was going to read an excerpt but then I thought what if you had the opportunity to write your own entry for the Grove Dictionary of Jazz? How would you use to describe your music? What would you say succinctly to sort of sum up your philosophy about music? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

Well music for me, playing music for me is to show forth the glory of God. Not by my power but by His power, and not for my glory but for His glory. And the concept is jazz. I’m a jazz musician. I’m an improviser. But in terms of music and why I am doing what I am doing, that was it.
Was your faith in place as a child before you became a professional musician?

Well I was raised — it’s interesting — my sister and I were raised in a home. My parents were married for I think six years before my mom passed. My dad was a Christian. My mom was Jewish — came from Russia, a Russian Jew. And so I went to Jewish temple in the beginning but then on the way to the Jewish Sunday School my dad would preach Christ to me. And when I got to the Jewish synagogue they didn’t want to hear about that. What it did, what it did, it gave me — something happened. They gave me the freedom of choice, where I wasn’t going to be manipulated to believe one way or another. Whatever happened, how ever the Lord intervened. Go ahead.
Do you think that that freedom of choice early on like that, with such an important subject, helped you form a way of being as a musician with making significant choices that would suit you?

Yeah. You know I think we’re all affected by what happens to us in life you know. Every little detail of how we live, you know, I was going to say imposes its way into our psyche. But that sounds a little negative. Everything we do in life, whether we’re shopping for groceries or whatever, inside this flesh is a spirit. And I’m no different now than when I’m playing music. It’s the same, it’s the same spirit. So whatever I collect in my life, when I’m not playing my instrument, comes out when I am playing my instrument.

You know Maria Schneider said something along those lines. She encouraged her students to not be so one-sided about just music, like live your life. And you have to be a full person in order to create something meaningful.

Yeah. That’s right. In my situation when I became a — when I made a commitment to Christianity, to Christ, then there’s a Scripture that says, “I know my sheep and my sheep know my voice, and no man can pluck them out of my hand.” My life was following the Lord and so I could do choices I made I could make with confidence in my life. It wasn’t just half-assed, or, there was, Jesus is called the light of the world. So you know I don’t think of my faith as a feeling. When I think of feeling I think of a blind man reaching out feeling his way through life. But Christ is called the light of the world so when the light’s turned on I can see where I’m walking. I can see where I’m going.
